newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Monde says Air France deals to boost access.
newsitem.headline: Le Monde says Air France deals to boost access.

text.p: Afternoon daily Le Monde, reporting a planned tie-up between Air France and both Continental and Delta Airlines, said the deals would involve so-called code sharing, and a variety of joint marketing and sales programmes.
The alliances would also include preferential quotas on partner airlines and would provide a base for the two U.S. airlines at Air France's Charles de Gaulle airport hub in Paris.
There would also be mutual maintenance agreements, it said.
Le Monde said the French state carrier would announce the two reported alliances later on Wednesday.
Air France had no immediate comment.

Industry sources say "code-sharing," or issuing a ticket common to more than one airline, is seen as a vital and cost-effective way of extending market access as airlines increasingly forge new alliances.
Le Monde said the tie-up would give Air France passengers "considerably improved" access to U.S. domestic routes from the summer of 1997.
